title: Capture a want in its source wording
summary: Preserve one supplied want and its source reference as durable Conatus intake for later organization in its Annals library.
use_when: The user expresses a want that should be preserved exactly and related to subsequent decisions.
do_not_use_when: The input is only an assistant suggestion or hypothetical example.
The requested outcome is task planning, inferred qualification extraction, immediate implementation, or a model examination.
outcome: One local immutable intake document records the want wording and source reference, awaiting update.
effects: Writes one local want intake record and its frozen outgoing document.
Does not enqueue, run a model, or change an Annals corpus.
authority: The user source defines the want. Conatus owns capture and provenance. Annals later owns retained library interpretation.
success: The capture receipt identifies the committed local want record.
failure_and_recovery: An input or storage error does not establish capture. Inspect the returned error before supplying a corrected input.
privacy: The full wording and source reference remain in local Conatus state. Later update can provide them to Annals and its model integration.
does_not_authorize: Publishing private content, directly editing Annals state, or changing unrelated product state.

access.statement: The current local user invokes the Conatus CLI. --state-dir selects private Conatus state. No remote API or multi-user authorization surface is provided.

compatibility_and_evolution.statement: Contract version 1 describes Conatus 0.1.0 public semantics independently of Annals, feed, library schema, or Clockwork versions.
No general cross-release compatibility or deprecation window is promised.

operational_limits.statement: Storage capacity and wall-clock completion bounds are not specified.

consumers.statement: A local user or agent captures one actual user-authored want from conversation or another identified source.

preconditions.statement: Conatus state is initialized and writable. The caller supplies one nonblank UTF-8 statement and its source-reference string.

inputs.statement: Exactly one text argument, --file input, or --stdin stream, plus --source text. File and stream transport do not authorize source modification.

outputs.statement: JSON {ok:true,data:...} returns the committed intake record. Errors use {ok:false,error:string}.

data_semantics.statement: Want wording is retained exactly. The source reference is opaque caller-supplied text and is not fetched or verified. No conditions, deadlines, priorities, lifecycle fields, or additional wants are inferred.

identity_and_units.statement: Want intake IDs use want- followed by a UUIDv7. captured_at is the UTC Unix-second time of local capture, not source authorship. The work name is the intake ID; the outgoing filename adds .md.

completeness_and_freshness.statement: A successful capture reports the locally committed complete wording and source reference. It does not establish Annals enqueue, work retention, or interpretation.

lifecycle_and_consistency.statement: Capture commits local intake and its frozen outgoing document. A later update forwards pending documents. Capture runs no model and does not change the Annals graph.

reliances.statement: Capture writes only Conatus local state and invokes no model, Annals, or network service.
